  <h1>Release notes</h1>
  <p class="inner-page__subtitle">How emissivity.org is built and what changed in each release, written for whoever maintains the site next. Additions visible to visitors are listed on <a href="/changelog.html">What's new</a>. Last updated 2026-10-01.</p>
  <p>The site is a Quarto website deployed by Netlify from the <code>main</code> branch. Data-driven pages are generated at build time from the YAML files in <code>_data/</code> by the scripts in <code>tools/</code>; the build order is in <code>tools/netlify-build.sh</code>. The repository README lists every data source and the routine maintenance commands.</p>
  <div class="release">
    <h2><span class="release-version">v3.5</span> Training section, upcoming-event highlight, &#x27;new&#x27; mark on News <span class="log-date-inline">2026-10-01</span></h2>
    <h3>What changed</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>Training section at /training/ with its own navbar entry: hub page, listing of training items plus the existing schools, item template and new_entry.py support.</li>
      <li>Events dated today or later are drawn as a highlighted box in every listing (events index, conference archive, schools, training), burgundy accent.</li>
      <li>The News link in the navbar carries a small pulsing dot for 14 days after the newest news post.</li>
    </ul>
    <h3>How it was done</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>Upcoming highlight: assets/includes/upcoming-events.html (include-after-body) reads the data-listing-date-sort epoch that Quarto puts on every listing item and adds the class &#x27;upcoming&#x27;; the box is styled in theme.css under .quarto-post.upcoming. Evaluated in the browser so it stays right between deploys.</li>
      <li>News mark: tools/generate_changelog.py scans events-news/news/*.qmd (skipping drafts) and stamps the newest date into data-latest-news on the News link, between the latest-news markers in assets/includes/site-header.html. A script at the end of the header shows the dot when that date is within 14 days; CSS pulses it 8 times (about 11 s) then holds; on news pages it is steady; reduced-motion users get no animation.</li>
      <li>Training: training/index.qmd lists training/items/*.qmd and events-news/schools/*.qmd in one listing. Items use the frontmatter in training/items/_template.qmd (kind, format, organiser, level, fee, registration_deadline). Nav link in site-header.html, footer link, card on events-news/index.qmd.</li>
      <li>New colour token --burgundy (#7a1f2b) for attention accents, alongside --brass for the featured band.</li>
    </ul>
    <h3>Files to know</h3>
    <ul class="release-files">

      <li><code>assets/includes/upcoming-events.html</code></li>
      <li><code>training/index.qmd, training/items/_template.qmd</code></li>
      <li><code>tools/generate_changelog.py (stamp_header, latest_news_date)</code></li>
      <li><code>tools/new_entry.py (training)</code></li>
    </ul>

  <div class="release">
    <h2><span class="release-version">v3.4</span> Changelog, release notes, last-updated stamp <span class="log-date-inline">2026-10-01</span></h2>
    <h3>What changed</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>Public &#x27;What&#x27;s new&#x27; page listing every addition to the site.</li>
      <li>Release notes page for maintainers.</li>
      <li>&#x27;Last updated&#x27; stamp in the footer, linking to What&#x27;s new.</li>
      <li>RISEnergy access call news item; IETcc-CSIC database on the data-resources page.</li>
    </ul>
    <h3>How it was done</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>Two hand-maintained data files, _data/changelog.yml and _data/releases.yml, are the only sources of truth.</li>
      <li>tools/generate_changelog.py renders them into changelog.qmd and about/release-notes.qmd and rewrites the marked region of assets/includes/site-footer.html with the newest date. It runs in tools/netlify-build.sh with the other generators.</li>
      <li>The stamp date is the newest entry date across both files, so a release or an addition updates it without a separate edit.</li>
    </ul>
    <h3>Files to know</h3>
    <ul class="release-files">

    </ul>

  <div class="release">
    <h2><span class="release-version">v3.3</span> Content audit, MathJax, measured home figure <span class="log-date-inline">2026-09-29</span></h2>
    <h3>What changed</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>45 corrections from a five-part review of every content source: citations and DOIs, standards scopes, EKHI descriptions, institution facts, events archive, privacy and contribution pages.</li>
      <li>Mathematics typeset site-wide; measurement-principles page rewritten with formulas.</li>
      <li>Home-page figure built from measured EKHI data (de Vos 1954 tungsten) instead of a hand-drawn curve.</li>
      <li>Display equations constrained to the paragraph measure.</li>
    </ul>
    <h3>How it was done</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>MathJax 3 is loaded on every page from assets/includes/mathjax.html (include-in-header in _quarto.yml), with backslash-parenthesis inline and backslash-bracket display delimiters (dollar signs are off), because site pages are raw-HTML blocks that Quarto never scans for math. Pages that must show those delimiters literally need the nomath class.</li>
      <li>The home figure is generated: _data/hero-spectrum.yml holds the measured points and provenance; tools/generate_hero_figure.py renders _hero-spectrum.qmd (SVG plus caption), included by index.qmd.</li>
      <li>Only 18 of the 49 network profiles are regenerated by tools/generate_network.py from _data/institutions.yml; the rest are hand-written and must be edited directly when the YAML changes.</li>
      <li>Audit corrections were committed one section at a time so each is reviewable in git history (commits 31061cb to 709c8f9).</li>
    </ul>
    <h3>Files to know</h3>
    <ul class="release-files">
      <li><code>assets/includes/mathjax.html</code></li>
      <li><code>_data/hero-spectrum.yml, tools/generate_hero_figure.py, _hero-spectrum.qmd</code></li>
      <li><code>methods/principles.qmd (unlisted page; formulas in LaTeX)</code></li>
    </ul>
  </div>
  <div class="release">
    <h2><span class="release-version">v3.2</span> Post-workshop update: IR-EMPOWER 2026, networks, schools, map basemap <span class="log-date-inline">2026-09-25</span></h2>
    <h3>What changed</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>IR-EMPOWER 2026 section generated from data: programme, speakers, committee, round table, award, talk BibTeX.</li>
      <li>Research networks pages (TAMARYS, PaRaMetriC) and a schools &amp; courses page.</li>
      <li>Six institutions added to the research map (46 in total).</li>
      <li>Research map drawn on an OpenFreeMap vector basemap (CARTO tiles now need an API key).</li>
      <li>iCal feed generated from _data/calendar.yml.</li>
      <li>Site-at-a-glance infographic on the About page.</li>
    </ul>
    <h3>How it was done</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>tools/generate_ir_empower.py renders _data/ir-empower.yml into ir-empower/2026/*.qmd and files/bib/ir-empower-2026.bib.</li>
      <li>tools/generate_ical.py renders _data/calendar.yml into files/ical/emissivity-conferences.ics; the calendar page itself is built from events-news/conferences/*.qmd, so an event must be added in both places.</li>
      <li>assets/scripts/labs-map.js loads MapLibre GL through the maplibre-gl-leaflet bridge and the OpenFreeMap Positron style, falling back to OpenStreetMap raster tiles. The script tag carries a ?v= query that must be bumped when the script changes, because browsers cache it.</li>
      <li>Netlify build image is Noble; Python is pinned to 3.12 in netlify.toml because the image&#x27;s installer refuses 3.8. Assets are served with max-age=0, must-revalidate.</li>
      <li>The analytics page and the header include name the exact third-party hosts contacted (Google Fonts, jsDelivr, cdnjs).</li>
    </ul>
    <h3>Files to know</h3>
    <ul class="release-files">
      <li><code>_data/ir-empower.yml, tools/generate_ir_empower.py</code></li>
      <li><code>_data/calendar.yml, tools/generate_ical.py</code></li>
      <li><code>_data/networks.yml, tools/generate_network.py</code></li>
      <li><code>assets/scripts/labs-map.js</code></li>
      <li><code>netlify.toml, tools/netlify-build.sh</code></li>
    </ul>
  </div>

      <li>GoatCounter is loaded from assets/includes/fonts.html; it sets no cookies.</li>
    </ul>
    <h3>Files to know</h3>
    <ul class="release-files">

      <li><code>ir-empower/2024/</code></li>

  <div class="release">
    <h2><span class="release-version">v3.0</span> Standalone site repository <span class="log-date-inline">2026-06-11</span></h2>
    <h3>What changed</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>emissivity.org rebuilt as a Quarto website with theme: none and the family design kit, deployed by Netlify from the main branch.</li>
    </ul>
    <h3>How it was done</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>No base directory: the repository root is the Quarto project. Netlify runs bash tools/netlify-build.sh, which installs Quarto, runs the Python generators, renders to _site, and copies assets/data and assets/scripts.</li>
      <li>Content pages are raw-HTML blocks inside .qmd files sharing assets/styles/theme.css; data-driven pages are generated from _data/*.yml by scripts in tools/.</li>
    </ul>
    <h3>Files to know</h3>
    <ul class="release-files">
      <li><code>_quarto.yml, netlify.toml, tools/netlify-build.sh</code></li>
      <li><code>assets/styles/theme.css</code></li>
      <li><code>README.md (data sources table and routine maintenance)</code></li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</div>
